title: Elodie and the Promise
premise: Sable Voss, a cellist whose hands froze mid-concert a year ago, retreats to a derelict orchard left to her by her grandmother, only to discover the deed also bears the name of Wren Calloway—the childhood friend she abandoned to pursue fame, and the one person who knows why Sable's music died. Forced into uneasy co-ownership, they restore the orchard together while old wounds and unspoken love surface. When developers threaten the land and Wren's own secret illness emerges, Sable must finally speak the rehearsed sentence—'I chose the stage over you, and I was wrong'—choosing love over the survival instinct that kept her invisible.
about_author: Zephyrine Sterling is the pen name of a former orchestral librarian who spent fifteen years backstage before turning to fiction. They write quiet, music-soaked romances about people learning that vulnerability is not defeat.

chapters.title: The Deed with Two Names
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Arriving at the crumbling orchard after her catastrophic final performance, Sable discovers Wren's name beside hers on the deed. The shock reopens a decade-old wound. Emotional beat: dread disguised as practical annoyance; Sable resolves to buy Wren out quickly and stay invisible again.

chapters.title: Frost on the First Branches
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren arrives expecting a fight, armed with a lawyer's letter and ten years of resentment. Instead they find Sable smaller, quieter, her hands bandaged from nervous scratching. Emotional beat: guarded tenderness; Wren agrees to one month of shared stewardship before deciding the deed's fate.

chapters.title: What the Cellar Kept
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Clearing the root cellar, they uncover grandmother's letters revealing she knew about their falling-out—and engineered the shared inheritance deliberately. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity; both begin wondering whether the old woman saw something in them they refuse to see themselves.

chapters.title: Grafting Season
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Teaching Sable grafting, Wren watches her hands steady for the first time since the concert. A near-touch over a sapling goes unacknowledged. Emotional beat: warming intimacy shadowed by denial; Wren hides a hospital letter in the barn loft.

chapters.title: The Rehearsed Sentence
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A storm traps them indoors; Sable almost says the sentence she has rehearsed for ten years—I chose the stage over you—but deflects into an argument about abandonment. Emotional beat: rising tension; the reader learns the full story of the betrayal night.

chapters.title: Developers at the Gate
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A land developer offers a fortune for the orchard, exploiting the disputed deed. Wren, facing mounting medical bills, is tempted. Emotional beat: external pressure crystallizes internal conflict; money versus memory, survival versus love.

chapters.title: One Cello, Unplayed
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable finds Wren's diagnosis hidden in the loft and realizes Wren came back not for the deed but to die near home. She plays the cello for the first time in a year—badly, weeping. Emotional beat: shattering of containment; the heart refuses to stay a muscle.

chapters.title: The Auction Notice
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Believing Sable will sell and leave as she always does, Wren signs the auction papers alone—a mirror of the original betrayal. Sable discovers it. Emotional beat: climax of misunderstanding; both choose self-protection at the exact moment honesty was possible.

chapters.title: Say It Before the Frost
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On auction morning, before the assembled buyers, Sable plays the piece she abandoned mid-performance and speaks the rehearsed sentence aloud, publicly choosing Wren over the stage forever. Wren tears up the papers. Emotional beat: cathartic climax; love declared against every survival instinct.

chapters.title: Blossom After Hard Winter
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Spring: the orchard blooms, Wren begins treatment with Sable beside them, and Sable teaches cello to local children rather than performing. The final line of grandmother's last letter is read at last. Emotional beat: resolution; identity rebuilt not around hiding or fame, but around chosen love.
